newsitem.title: TURKEY: Heavy-smoking Turkey bans public use of tobacco.
newsitem.headline: Heavy-smoking Turkey bans public use of tobacco.

text.p: Major tobacco producer Turkey's millions of smokers woke up on Tuesday to a ban by the Islamist-led government on smoking in public places.
A law printed in the Official Gazette forbids use of tobacco in public buildings, workplaces with six or more employees, and on public transport.
Smokers who light up in defiance of the ban face fines of 10 million lira ($100) if they do not stub out after a warning.

Special smoking areas are to be set aside in enclosed public places. Smoking in Turkey, more socially acceptable than in the West, is widespread but exact figures of those addicted to nicotine are not available.
Non-smoking households often display a tray of foreign and Turkish cigarettes to offer guests.
